questions.text: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^2-x+p=0$ and $\gamma, \delta$ be the roots the equation $x^2-4x+q=0$; $p, q \in \mathbb{Z}$. If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are in G.P., then $|p+q|$ equals :
questions.sol:
Let the G.P. be $\alpha, \alpha r, \alpha r^2, \alpha r^3$.
$\alpha+\beta=\alpha(1+r)=1$ and $\gamma+\delta=\alpha r^2(1+r)=4$, so $r^2=4$, $r=\pm2$.
$r=2$: $\alpha=\dfrac13$, $p=\alpha\beta=\dfrac29\notin\mathbb{Z}$, rejected.
$r=-2$: $\alpha=-1$, terms $-1, 2, -4, 8$; $p=-2$, $q=(-4)(8)=-32$.
$|p+q|=34$.

questions.text: If $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is defined by $$f(n)=\begin{vmatrix} n & -1 & -5 \\ -2n^2 & 3(2k+1) & 2k+1 \\ -3n^3 & 3k(2k+1) & 3k(k+2)+1 \end{vmatrix},\ k\in\mathbb{N},$$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k} f(n)=98$, then $k$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Only the first column depends on $n$, so $\sum_{n=1}^k f(n)$ is the determinant with first column $\left(\sum n,\ -2\sum n^2,\ -3\sum n^3\right)=\left(\dfrac{k(k+1)}{2},\ -\dfrac{k(k+1)(2k+1)}{3},\ -\dfrac{3k^2(k+1)^2}{4}\right)$.
For $k=3$ the first column is $(6, -28, -108)$ and the determinant is $\begin{vmatrix} 6 & -1 & -5 \\ -28 & 21 & 7 \\ -108 & 63 & 46 \end{vmatrix}$.
$=6(966-441)+1(-1288+756)-5(-1764+2268)=3150-532-2520=98$.
Hence $k=3$.

questions.text: Let M be a $3\times3$ matrix such that $$M\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{pmatrix},\ M\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\2\end{pmatrix} \text{ and } M\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}.$$ If $M\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\7\\11\end{pmatrix}$, then $x+y+z$ equals :
questions.sol:
The given products are the columns of $M$: $M=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\2&1&1\\3&2&1\end{pmatrix}$.
So $x-z=1$, $2x+y+z=7$, $3x+2y+z=11$.
Subtracting the last two: $x+y=4$. With $x=1+z$: $y=3-z$ and $2(1+z)+(3-z)+z=7 \Rightarrow z=1$.
$x=2$, $y=2$, $z=1$, so $x+y+z=5$.

questions.text: If the sum of the first 10 terms of the series $$\dfrac{1}{1+1^4\times4}+\dfrac{2}{1+2^4\times4}+\dfrac{3}{1+3^4\times4}+\dfrac{4}{1+4^4\times4}+\ldots$$ is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$1+4n^4=(2n^2+2n+1)(2n^2-2n+1)$, and the difference of these factors is $4n$.
So $T_n=\dfrac{n}{1+4n^4}=\dfrac14\left[\dfrac{1}{2n^2-2n+1}-\dfrac{1}{2n^2+2n+1}\right]$.
Since $2(n+1)^2-2(n+1)+1=2n^2+2n+1$, the sum telescopes: $S_{10}=\dfrac14\left[1-\dfrac{1}{221}\right]=\dfrac{55}{221}$.
$\gcd(55,221)=1$, so $m+n=276$.

questions.text: Let $A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots, A_{39}$ be 39 arithmetic means between the numbers 59 and 159. Then the mean of $A_{25}, A_{28}, A_{31}$ and $A_{36}$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
There are 41 terms in all, so $d=\dfrac{159-59}{40}=2.5$ and $A_k=59+2.5k$.
Mean of the four $=59+2.5\times\dfrac{25+28+31+36}{4}=59+2.5\times30=134$.

questions.text: A variable X takes values $0, 0, 2, 6, 12, 20, \ldots, n(n-1)$ with frequencies ${}^nC_0, {}^nC_1, {}^nC_2, {}^nC_3, {}^nC_4, {}^nC_5, \ldots, {}^nC_n$, respectively. If the mean of this data is 60, then its median is :
questions.sol:
The value $r(r-1)$ has frequency ${}^nC_r$. $\sum r(r-1){}^nC_r=n(n-1)2^{n-2}$ and $\sum{}^nC_r=2^n$.
Mean $=\dfrac{n(n-1)}{4}=60 \Rightarrow n(n-1)=240 \Rightarrow n=16$.
Values increase with $r$ and the frequencies ${}^{16}C_r$ are symmetric about $r=8$, so the middle observations (the $2^{15}$-th and next) both fall at $r=8$.
Median $=8\times7=56$.

questions.text: Let the point P be the vertex of the parabola $y=x^2-6x+12$. If a line passing through the point P intersects the circle $x^2+y^2-2x-4y+3=0$ at the points R and S, then the maximum value of $(PR+PS)^2$ is :
questions.sol:
$y=(x-3)^2+3$, so $P=(3,3)$. Circle: centre $C=(1,2)$, radius $\sqrt2$; $CP=\sqrt5>\sqrt2$, so P is outside.
For a line through P at angle $\theta$ to PC, R and S are symmetric about the foot of the perpendicular from C, so $PR+PS=2\,CP\cos\theta$.
Maximum when the line passes through C: $PR+PS=2\sqrt5$.
$(PR+PS)^2=20$.

questions.text: Let the directrix of the parabola $P: y^2=8x$, cut $x$-axis at the point A. Let $B(\alpha,\beta)$, $\alpha>1$, be a point on P such that the slope of AB is $3/5$. If BC is a focal chord of P, then six times the area of $\Delta ABC$ is :
questions.sol:
$a=2$: directrix $x=-2$, so $A=(-2,0)$. Let $B=(2t^2,4t)$.
Slope $\dfrac{4t}{2t^2+2}=\dfrac35 \Rightarrow 3t^2-10t+3=0 \Rightarrow t=3$ or $\dfrac13$; $\alpha=2t^2>1$ gives $t=3$, $B=(18,12)$.
Focal chord: C has parameter $-\dfrac1t=-\dfrac13$, $C=\left(\dfrac29,-\dfrac43\right)$.
$\vec{AB}=(20,12)$, $\vec{AC}=\left(\dfrac{20}{9},-\dfrac43\right)$; area $=\dfrac12\left|20\left(-\dfrac43\right)-12\cdot\dfrac{20}{9}\right|=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{160}{3}=\dfrac{80}{3}$.
Six times the area $=160$.

questions.text: Let the eccentricity e of a hyperbola satisfy the equation $6e^2-11e+3=0$. If the foci of the hyperbola are $(3,5)$ and $(3,-4)$, then the length of its latus rectum is :
questions.sol:
$6e^2-11e+3=0 \Rightarrow e=\dfrac32$ or $\dfrac13$; for a hyperbola $e=\dfrac32$.
Distance between foci $2ae=9 \Rightarrow a=3$.
$b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=9\cdot\dfrac54=\dfrac{45}{4}$.
Latus rectum $=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{45/2}{3}=\dfrac{15}{2}$.

questions.text: Let a triangle PQR be such that P and Q lie on the line $\dfrac{x+3}{8}=\dfrac{y-4}{2}=\dfrac{z+1}{2}$ and are at a distance of 6 units from $R(1,2,3)$. If $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ is the centroid of $\Delta PQR$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Since $RP=RQ$, the midpoint of PQ is the foot M of the perpendicular from R to the line.
Point on line: $(-3+8t, 4+2t, -1+2t)$; $(4-8t, -2-2t, 4-2t)\cdot(8,2,2)=36-72t=0 \Rightarrow t=\dfrac12$, $M=(1,5,0)$ (and $RM=\sqrt{18}<6$).
Centroid $=\dfrac{P+Q+R}{3}=\dfrac{2M+R}{3}=\dfrac{(3,12,3)}{3}=(1,4,1)$.
$\alpha+\beta+\gamma=6$.

questions.text: Let O be the origin, $\vec{OP}=\vec{a}$ and $\vec{OQ}=\vec{b}$. If R is the point on $\vec{OP}$ such that $\vec{OP}=5\vec{OR}$, and M is the point such that $\vec{OQ}=5\vec{RM}$, then $\vec{PM}$ is equal to :

$\vec{OR}=\dfrac{\vec a}{5}$ and $\vec{RM}=\dfrac{\vec b}{5}$, so $\vec{OM}=\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b}{5}$.
$\vec{PM}=\vec{OM}-\vec{OP}=\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b}{5}-\vec a=\dfrac15\left(\vec b-4\vec a\right)$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{y\to0}\dfrac{(1-\cos(xy))\tan(xy)}{y^3}$. Then the number of solutions of the equation $f(x)=\sin x$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$ is :
questions.sol:
With $u=xy$: $(1-\cos u)\tan u\approx\dfrac{u^2}{2}\cdot u=\dfrac{x^3y^3}{2}$, so $f(x)=\dfrac{x^3}{2}$.
Solve $\dfrac{x^3}{2}=\sin x$. $x=0$ is a root. For small $x>0$, $\dfrac{x^3}{2}<\sin x$; at $x=1.5$, $\dfrac{x^3}{2}\approx1.69>\sin x$; for $x>\sqrt[3]{2}$, $\dfrac{x^3}{2}>1\ge\sin x$. So exactly one positive root.
Both sides are odd, giving one negative root too.
Number of solutions $=3$.

questions.text: Let $(2^{1-a}+2^{1+a})$, $f(a)$, $(3^a+3^{-a})$ be in A.P. and $\alpha$ be the minimum value of $f(a)$. Then the value of the integral $\displaystyle\int_{\log_e(\alpha-1)}^{\log_e(\alpha)}\dfrac{dx}{(e^{2x}-e^{-2x})}$ is :
questions.sol:
$f(a)=\dfrac{2(2^a+2^{-a})+(3^a+3^{-a})}{2}\ge\dfrac{4+2}{2}=3$ (equality at $a=0$), so $\alpha=3$.
$I=\displaystyle\int_{\ln2}^{\ln3}\dfrac{e^{2x}\,dx}{e^{4x}-1}$. Put $u=e^{2x}$, $du=2u\,dx$: $I=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_4^9\dfrac{du}{u^2-1}=\dfrac14\left[\ln\dfrac{u-1}{u+1}\right]_4^9$.
$=\dfrac14\left(\ln\dfrac45-\ln\dfrac35\right)=\dfrac14\log_e\left(\dfrac43\right)$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:[1,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function defined as $f(x)=\displaystyle\int_1^x f(t)\,dt+(1-x)(\log_e x-1)+e$. Then the value of $f(f(1))$ is :
questions.sol:
$f(1)=0+0+e=e$.
Differentiating: $f'(x)=f(x)-(\ln x-1)+\dfrac{1-x}{x}=f(x)-\ln x+\dfrac1x$.
So $f'-f=\dfrac1x-\ln x$; $\ln x$ is a particular solution (since $(\ln x)'-\ln x=\dfrac1x-\ln x$), hence $f(x)=\ln x+Ce^x$.
$f(1)=Ce=e \Rightarrow C=1$, so $f(x)=\ln x+e^x$.
$f(f(1))=f(e)=1+e^e$.

questions.text: Let $A=\{1,4,7\}$ and $B=\{2,3,8\}$. Then the number of elements, in the relation $R=\{((a_1,b_1),(a_2,b_2))\in((A\times B)\times(A\times B)) : a_1+b_2 \text{ divides } a_2+b_1\}$ is __________.
questions.sol:
As $(a_1,b_2)$ runs over $A\times B$, $s=a_1+b_2$ takes the values $3,4,9,6,7,12,9,10,15$; independently $t=a_2+b_1$ takes the same 9 values.
Count pairs with $s\mid t$: $s=3$: 6 values of $t$ ($3,9,6,12,9,15$); $s=4$: 2 ($4,12$); $s=9$ (twice): $2\times2=4$; $s=6$: 2 ($6,12$); $s=7,12,10,15$: 1 each.
Total $=6+2+4+2+4=18$.

questions.text: From the point $(-1,-1)$, two rays are sent making angles of $45^\circ$ with the line $x+y=0$. These rays get reflected from the mirror $x+2y=1$. If the equations of the reflected rays are $ax+by=9$ and $cx+dy=7$, $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{Z}$, then the value of $ad+bc$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Lines through $(-1,-1)$ at $45^\circ$ to $x+y=0$ are $y=-1$ and $x=-1$. They meet the mirror at $(3,-1)$ and $(-1,1)$.
Each reflected ray passes through the image of $(-1,-1)$ in $x+2y-1=0$: $(-1,-1)-\dfrac{2(-4)}{5}(1,2)=\left(\dfrac35,\dfrac{11}{5}\right)$.
Through $(3,-1)$: slope $-\dfrac43$, line $4x+3y=9$, so $a=4$, $b=3$.
Through $(-1,1)$: slope $\dfrac34$, line $-3x+4y=7$, so $c=-3$, $d=4$.
$ad+bc=16-9=7$.

questions.text: If $S=\left\{\theta\in[-\pi,\pi] : \cos\theta\cos\dfrac{5\theta}{2}=\cos7\theta\cos\dfrac{7\theta}{2}\right\}$, then $n(S)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Multiply by 2: $\cos\dfrac{7\theta}{2}+\cos\dfrac{3\theta}{2}=\cos\dfrac{21\theta}{2}+\cos\dfrac{7\theta}{2}$, so $\cos\dfrac{21\theta}{2}=\cos\dfrac{3\theta}{2}$.
$\dfrac{21\theta}{2}=2n\pi\pm\dfrac{3\theta}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\dfrac{2n\pi}{9}$ or $\theta=\dfrac{n\pi}{6}$.
In $[-\pi,\pi]$: $\dfrac{2n\pi}{9}$, $n=-4,\ldots,4$: 9 values; $\dfrac{n\pi}{6}$, $n=-6,\ldots,6$: 13 values.
Common: $0,\pm\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ (3 values).
$n(S)=9+13-3=19$.

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $f(x)+3f\left(\dfrac\pi2-x\right)=\sin x$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let the maximum value of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$ be $\alpha$. If the area of the region bounded by the curves $g(x)=x^2$ and $h(x)=\beta x^3$, $\beta>0$, is $\alpha^2$, then $30\beta^3$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac\pi2-x$: $f\left(\dfrac\pi2-x\right)+3f(x)=\cos x$.
Solving the two equations: $f(x)=\dfrac{3\cos x-\sin x}{8}$, so $\alpha=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{8}$ and $\alpha^2=\dfrac{5}{32}$.
Curves meet at $x=0$ and $x=\dfrac1\beta$: area $=\displaystyle\int_0^{1/\beta}(x^2-\beta x^3)\,dx=\dfrac{1}{3\beta^3}-\dfrac{1}{4\beta^3}=\dfrac{1}{12\beta^3}$.
$\dfrac{1}{12\beta^3}=\dfrac{5}{32} \Rightarrow \beta^3=\dfrac{8}{15}$.
$30\beta^3=16$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $$(\tan x)^{1/2}\,dy=\left(\sec^3x-(\tan x)^{3/2}\,y\right)dx,\quad 0<x<\dfrac\pi2,\quad y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)=\dfrac{6\sqrt2}{5}.$$ If $y\left(\dfrac\pi3\right)=\dfrac45\alpha$, then $\alpha^4$ equals __________.
questions.sol:
Dividing by $\sqrt{\tan x}$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=\dfrac{\sec^3x}{\sqrt{\tan x}}$. Integrating factor $\sec x$.
$y\sec x=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sec^4x}{\sqrt{\tan x}}dx=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1+t^2}{\sqrt t}dt=2\sqrt t+\dfrac25t^{5/2}+C$, with $t=\tan x$.
At $x=\dfrac\pi4$: $\dfrac{6\sqrt2}{5}\cdot\sqrt2=\dfrac{12}{5}=2+\dfrac25+C \Rightarrow C=0$.
At $x=\dfrac\pi3$ ($t=\sqrt3$, $\sec x=2$): $2y=3^{1/4}\left(2+\dfrac65\right)=\dfrac{16}{5}3^{1/4}$, so $y=\dfrac85 3^{1/4}=\dfrac45\alpha$.
$\alpha=2\cdot3^{1/4}$, $\alpha^4=48$.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
A. Meter (L)I. $\sqrt{\dfrac{hc}{G}}$
B. Second (S)II. $\sqrt{\dfrac{Gh}{c^5}}$
C. Kilogram (M)III. $\sqrt{\dfrac{K^2L^2c^3}{Gh}}$
D. Kelvin (K)IV. $\sqrt{\dfrac{Gh}{c^3}}$
where h (Planck's constant), G (gravitational constant) and c (speed of light in vacuum) as fundamental units.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Dimensions: $[h]=ML^2T^{-1}$, $[G]=M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}$, $[c]=LT^{-1}$.
$\dfrac{Gh}{c^3}$ has dimensions $L^2$, so length $\propto\sqrt{\dfrac{Gh}{c^3}}$ (A-IV).
Time $=\dfrac{\text{length}}{c}\propto\sqrt{\dfrac{Gh}{c^5}}$ (B-II).
$\dfrac{hc}{G}$ has dimensions $M^2$, so mass $\propto\sqrt{\dfrac{hc}{G}}$ (C-I).
The remaining expression III goes with Kelvin (D-III).
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: In an experiment to determine the resistance of a given wire using Ohm's law, the voltmeter and ammeter readings are noted as 10 V and 5 A, respectively. The least counts of voltmeter and ammeter are 500 mV and 200 mA, respectively. The estimated error in the resistance measurement is __________ $\Omega$
questions.sol:
$R=\dfrac{V}{I}=\dfrac{10}{5}=2\ \Omega$.
$\dfrac{\Delta R}{R}=\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}+\dfrac{\Delta I}{I}=\dfrac{0.5}{10}+\dfrac{0.2}{5}=0.05+0.04=0.09$.
$\Delta R=0.09\times2=0.18\ \Omega$.

questions.text: A mass of 1 kg is kept on a inclined plane with $30^\circ$ inclination with respect to horizontal plane and it is at rest initially. Then the whole assembly is moved up with constant velocity of 4 m/s. The work done by the frictional force in time 2 s is __________ J. (Take $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
questions.sol:
The block stays at rest relative to the incline, and the assembly moves with constant velocity, so static friction balances the component of gravity along the incline: $f=mg\sin30^\circ=5$ N, directed up the incline.
In 2 s the block moves $4\times2=8$ m vertically upward.
Angle between the friction (along the incline, up) and the vertical displacement is $60^\circ$.
$W_f=5\times8\times\cos60^\circ=20$ J.

questions.text: The velocity $(v)$ versus time $(t)$ plot of a particle is shown in the figure, for a time interval of 40 s. The total distance travelled by the particle and the average velocity during this period are, respectively __________.
questions.sol:
Distance = total area between the graph and the time axis.
0 to 20 s: triangle of base 20 s and height 5 m/s, area $=50$ m (positive).
20 to 40 s: triangle of base 20 s and height 5 m/s below the axis, area $=50$ m (negative velocity).
Distance $=50+50=100$ m; displacement $=50-50=0$, so average velocity is zero.

questions.text: A wheel initially at rest is subjected to a uniform angular acceleration about its axis. In the first 2 s it rotates through an angle $\theta_1$ and in the next 2 s it rotates through an angle $\theta_2$. The ratio $\dfrac{\theta_2}{\theta_1}$ is __________.
questions.sol:
From rest, $\theta=\dfrac12\alpha t^2$.
$\theta_1=\dfrac12\alpha(2)^2=2\alpha$; $\theta_1+\theta_2=\dfrac12\alpha(4)^2=8\alpha \Rightarrow \theta_2=6\alpha$.
$\dfrac{\theta_2}{\theta_1}=3$.

questions.text: An object of uniform density rolls up the curved path with the initial velocity $v_o$ as shown in the figure. If the maximum height attained by an object is $\dfrac{7v_o^2}{10\,g}$ ($g$ = acceleration due to gravity), the object is a __________.
questions.sol:
Rolling without slipping: total KE $=\dfrac12mv_o^2\left(1+\dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right)$, all converted to $mgh$.
$h=\dfrac{v_o^2}{2g}\left(1+\dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right)=\dfrac{7v_o^2}{10g} \Rightarrow 1+\dfrac{k^2}{R^2}=\dfrac75 \Rightarrow \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}=\dfrac25$.
$k^2=\dfrac25R^2$ is a solid sphere.

questions.text:
A body of mass $m$ is taken from the surface of earth to a height equal to twice the radius of earth $(R_e)$. The increase in potential energy will be __________.
($g$ is acceleration due to gravity at the surface of earth)
questions.sol:
$\Delta U=GMm\left(\dfrac{1}{R_e}-\dfrac{1}{3R_e}\right)=\dfrac23\dfrac{GMm}{R_e}$.

questions.text: Eight mercury drops, each of radius $r$, coalesce to form a bigger drop. The surface energy released in this process is __________. (S is the surface tension of mercury).
questions.sol:
Volume conserved: $\dfrac43\pi R^3=8\cdot\dfrac43\pi r^3 \Rightarrow R=2r$.
Decrease in area $=8(4\pi r^2)-4\pi(2r)^2=32\pi r^2-16\pi r^2=16\pi r^2$.
Energy released $=16\pi r^2S$.

questions.text: An ideal gas at pressure $P$ and temperature $T$ is expanding such that $PT^3$ = constant. The coefficient of volume expansion of the gas is __________.
questions.sol:
$PV=nRT$ and $P\propto T^{-3}$, so $V\propto\dfrac{T}{P}\propto T^4$.
$\gamma=\dfrac1V\dfrac{dV}{dT}=\dfrac4T$.

Match List - I with List - II.

A. $\sin^2\omega t$I. Periodic with time period $T=\dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$ but not simple harmonic motion (SHM)
B. $\sin^3(2\omega t)$II. Periodic with time period $T=\dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$ but Not SHM
C. $\sin(\omega t)+\cos(\pi\omega t)$III. Periodic with time period $T=\dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$ and SHM

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

C: angular frequencies $\omega$ and $\pi\omega$ have an irrational ratio, so the sum is non-periodic → IV.
D: periods $\dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$, overall period $\dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$, not SHM → II.

questions.text: A metal rod of length $L$ rotates about one end at origin with a uniform angular velocity $\omega$. The magnetic field radially falls off as $B(r)=B_0e^{-\lambda r}$; $\lambda$ being a positive constant. The emf induced (neglecting the centripetal force on electrons in the rod) is :
questions.sol:
An element $dr$ at distance $r$ moves with speed $\omega r$: $d\varepsilon=B(r)\,\omega r\,dr$.
$\varepsilon=B_0\omega\displaystyle\int_0^L re^{-\lambda r}dr=B_0\omega\left[-\dfrac{re^{-\lambda r}}{\lambda}-\dfrac{e^{-\lambda r}}{\lambda^2}\right]_0^L$.
$=B_0\omega\left[\dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}-e^{-\lambda L}\left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}+\dfrac{L}{\lambda}\right)\right]$.

questions.text: Under steady state condition the potential difference across the capacitor in the circuit is __________ V.
questions.sol:
In steady state no current flows in the capacitor branch (capacitor + $4\ \Omega$).
Current in the loop of the 2 V cell, $6\ \Omega$ and $2\ \Omega$: $I=\dfrac{2}{6+2}=0.25$ A.
P.d. across the $2\ \Omega$ resistor (= p.d. across the capacitor branch) $=0.25\times2=0.5$ V; no drop across the $4\ \Omega$, so the capacitor has $0.5$ V.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A particle of charge $q$ and mass $m$ is projected from origin with an initial velocity $\vec{v}=\left(\dfrac{v_0}{\sqrt2}\hat{x}+\dfrac{v_0}{\sqrt2}\hat{y}\right)$. There exists a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}=B_0\hat{z}$ and a space varying electric field $\vec{E}=E_0e^{-\lambda x}\hat{x}$ within the region $0\le x\le L$. After travelling a distance such that $x$-coordinate has changed from $x=0$ to $x=L$, the change in the kinetic energy is __________.
questions.sol:
The magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity and does no work.
Work by the electric field: $W=\displaystyle\int_0^L qE_0e^{-\lambda x}dx=\dfrac{qE_0}{\lambda}\left[1-e^{-\lambda L}\right]$.
By the work-energy theorem this is the change in kinetic energy.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The electromagnetic wave exerts pressure on the surface on which they are allowed to fall.
Reason (R) : There is no mass associated with the electromagnetic waves.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
EM waves carry momentum $p=\dfrac{U}{c}$; when they fall on a surface, momentum is transferred, giving radiation pressure. (A) is true.
EM waves (photons) have no rest mass, so (R) is true.
But the pressure arises from the momentum carried by the wave, not from the absence of mass, so (R) does not explain (A).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thin convex lens and a thin concave lens are kept in contact and are co-axial. Which of the following statements is correct for this combination of two lenses ?
options: Focal length of the lens system will change if the positions of two lenses are interchanged
questions.sol:
Power of the combination: $P=\dfrac{1}{|f_{\text{convex}}|}-\dfrac{1}{|f_{\text{concave}}|}$.
If $|f_{\text{convex}}|>|f_{\text{concave}}|$, then $P<0$: the combination behaves as a concave (diverging) lens.
For thin lenses in contact, interchanging them does not change $P$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An object $AB$ is placed 15 cm on the left of a convex lens $P$ of focal length 10 cm. Another convex lens $Q$ is now placed 15 cm right of lens $P$. If the focal length of lens $Q$ is 15 cm, the final image is __________.
options: virtual, formed at 7.5 cm right of lens $Q$, with a size bigger than that of $AB$
real, formed at 7.5 cm right of lens $Q$, with a size same as that of $AB$
real, formed at 7 cm right of lens $Q$, with a size smaller than that of $AB$
questions.sol:
Lens P: $u=-15$, $f=10$: $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1{10}-\dfrac1{15}=\dfrac1{30} \Rightarrow v=30$ cm; $m_1=\dfrac{30}{-15}=-2$.
This image is 15 cm beyond Q, so it is a virtual object for Q: $u=+15$, $f=15$: $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1{15}+\dfrac1{15} \Rightarrow v=7.5$ cm; $m_2=\dfrac{7.5}{15}=\dfrac12$.
$m=m_1m_2=-1$: real (inverted) image 7.5 cm right of Q, same size as AB.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The maximum intensity in a Young's double slit experiment is $I_o$. Distance between the slits $(d)$ is $5\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light used. The intensity of the fringe, exactly opposite to one of the slits on the screen, placed at $D=10d$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Opposite a slit, $y=\dfrac d2$: path difference $=\dfrac{yd}{D}=\dfrac{d^2}{2D}=\dfrac{d}{20}=\dfrac{5\lambda}{20}=\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$.
Phase difference $\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\cdot\dfrac{\lambda}{4}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
$I=I_o\cos^2\dfrac{\phi}{2}=I_o\cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{4}=\dfrac{I_o}{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electron is travelling with a velocity $v$ in free space and when it enters a medium, its velocity is reduced by 20%. The de Broglie wavelength of electron in the medium is $\alpha\lambda_0$, where $\lambda_0$ is its de Broglie wavelength in free space. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.sol:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{mv}\propto\dfrac1v$.
In the medium $v'=0.8v$, so $\lambda=\dfrac{\lambda_0}{0.8}=1.25\lambda_0$.
$\alpha=1.25$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
Assuming the experimental mass of ${}^{12}_{6}C$ as 12 u, the mass defect of ${}^{12}_{6}C$ atom is __________ $\mathrm{MeV/c^2}$.
(Mass of proton = 1.00727 u. mass of neutron = 1.00866 u, 1 u = 931.5 $\mathrm{MeV/c^2}$ and c is the speed of the light in vacuum).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a semiconductor p-n diode, the doping concentrations on p-side and n-side are $10^{15}$ atoms/cm$^3$ and $10^{18}$ atoms/cm$^3$, respectively. Which one of the following statements is true ?
options: Widths of depletion region on either side of the interface are equal
The depletion region width is more on p-side compared to that in n-side
The depletion region width is more on n-side compared to that in p-side
No depletion region forms because of unequal doping concentrations on p and n-sides
questions.sol:
Charge neutrality of the depletion layer: $N_Ax_p=N_Dx_n$.
$\dfrac{x_p}{x_n}=\dfrac{N_D}{N_A}=\dfrac{10^{18}}{10^{15}}=1000$.
So the depletion region extends much more into the lightly doped p-side.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A copper wire of length 3 m is stretched by 3 mm by applying an external force. The volume of the wire is $600\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^3}$. The elastic potential energy stored in the wire in stretched condition would be __________ J.
(Given Young modulus of copper $=1.1\times10^{11}\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$)
questions.sol:
Strain $=\dfrac{3\times10^{-3}}{3}=10^{-3}$.
Energy $=\dfrac12Y(\text{strain})^2\times\text{volume}=\dfrac12\times1.1\times10^{11}\times10^{-6}\times600\times10^{-6}$.
$=33$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The heat extracted out of $x$ gram of water initially at $50\ {}^\circ$C to cool it down to $0\ {}^\circ$C is sufficient to evaporate $(1000-x)$ gram of water also initially at $50\ {}^\circ$C. The value of $x$ (closest integer) is __________.
(Take latent heat of water 2256 kJ/kg. K, specific heat capacity of water 4200 J/kg. K)
questions.sol:
Heat released by $x$ g cooling $50\to0\ {}^\circ$C: $x\times4.2\times50=210x$ J.
Heat to take $(1000-x)$ g from $50$ to $100\ {}^\circ$C and evaporate it: $(1000-x)(4.2\times50+2256)=2466(1000-x)$ J.
$210x=2466(1000-x) \Rightarrow x=\dfrac{2466000}{2676}\approx921.5$.
Closest integer: $922$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A series LCR circuit with $R=20\ \Omega$, $L=1.6$ H and $C=40\ \mu$F is connected to a variable frequency a.c. source. The inductive reactance at resonant frequency is __________ $\Omega$.
questions.sol:
$\omega_0=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1.6\times40\times10^{-6}}}=\dfrac{1}{8\times10^{-3}}=125$ rad/s.
$X_L=\omega_0L=125\times1.6=200\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: When an external resistance of $5\ \Omega$ is connected across terminals of a cell, a current of 0.25 A flows through it. When the $5\ \Omega$ resistor is replaced by a $2\ \Omega$ resistor, a current of 0.5 A flows through it. The internal resistance of the cell is __________ $\Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A circular loop of radius 20 cm and resistance $2\ \Omega$ is placed in a time varying magnetic field $\vec{B}=(2t^2+2t+3)$ T. At $t=0$, for the plane of the loop being perpendicular to the magnetic field and, the induced current in the loop at $t=3$ s is $\dfrac{\alpha}{50}$ A. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
(Take $\pi=22/7$)
questions.sol:
Flux $\phi=BA$ with $A=\pi(0.2)^2=0.04\pi\ \mathrm{m^2}$.
$\varepsilon=A\dfrac{dB}{dt}=0.04\pi(4t+2)$; at $t=3$ s: $\varepsilon=0.04\times\dfrac{22}{7}\times14=1.76$ V.
$I=\dfrac{1.76}{2}=0.88$ A $=\dfrac{44}{50}$ A.
$\alpha=44$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
What volume of hydrogen gas at STP would be liberated by action of 50 mL of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ of 50% purity (density $=1.3\ \mathrm{g\ mL^{-1}}$) on 20 g of zinc ?
Given : Molar mass of H, O, S, Zn are 1, 16, 32, 65 $\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$ respectively.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2}$.
Mass of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}=50\times1.3\times0.5=32.5$ g $=\dfrac{32.5}{98}=0.332$ mol.
Zn $=\dfrac{20}{65}=0.308$ mol, so Zn is limiting.
$V(\mathrm{H_2})=\dfrac{20}{65}\times22.4=6.892$ L.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true ?
A. If two orbitals have the same value of $(n+l)$, the orbital with lower value of n will have lower energy.
B. Energies of the orbitals in the same subshell increase with increase in atomic number.
C. The size of $2p_x$ orbital is less than the size of $3p_x$ orbital.
D. Among 5f, 6s, 4d, 5p and 5d orbitals, none of the orbitals have 2 radial nodes.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: true (the $(n+l)$ rule).
B: false; with increasing atomic number the effective nuclear charge increases and orbital energies decrease.
C: true; size increases with $n$.
D: radial nodes $=n-l-1$: 5f 1, 6s 5, 4d 1, 5p 3, 5d 2. The 5d orbital has 2 radial nodes, so D is false.
A and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The covalent radii of atoms A and B are $r_A$ and $r_B$, respectively. The covalent bond length and total length of AB molecule are respectively
questions.sol:
Bond length = distance between the two nuclei $=r_A+r_B$.
The total length of the molecule runs from the outer edge of A to the outer edge of B: $r_A+(r_A+r_B)+r_B=2(r_A+r_B)$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the following data for the reaction $\mathrm{X_2(g)+Y_2(g)\rightleftharpoons 2XY(g)}$ at 600 K. The $\Delta_rG^\ominus$ (in $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$) for the reaction is :$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Compound} & \Delta_fH^\ominus_{600\,K}\ (\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}) & S^\ominus_{600\,K}\ (\mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}\ K^{-1}}) \\ \hline \mathrm{XY(g)} & 42 & 200 \\ \hline \mathrm{X_2(g)} & 8 & 140 \\ \hline \mathrm{Y_2(g)} & 80 & 250 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
questions.sol:
$\Delta_rH^\ominus=2(42)-(8+80)=-4\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$.
$\Delta_rS^\ominus=2(200)-(140+250)=10\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}K^{-1}}=0.010\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$.
$\Delta_rG^\ominus=\Delta_rH^\ominus-T\Delta_rS^\ominus=-4-600\times0.010=-10\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct order of molar heat capacities measured at 298 K and 1 bar is :
questions.sol:
Molar heat capacities ($C_p$, J $\mathrm{K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$) at 298 K: $\mathrm{Br_2(l)}\approx75.7$, Cu(s) $\approx24.4$, He(g) $=\dfrac52R\approx20.8$.
A polyatomic liquid has many more modes to store energy than a metal (Dulong-Petit $\approx3R$) or a monatomic gas.
Order: Bromine(l) > Copper(s) > Helium(g).

questions.text:
The reaction $\mathrm{A(g)\rightleftharpoons B(g)+C(g)}$ was initiated with the amount 'a' of A(g). At equilibrium it is found that the amount of A(g) remaining is $(a-x)$ at a total pressure of p.
The equilibrium constant Kp of the reaction can be calculated from the expression :
questions.sol:
At equilibrium: A $=a-x$, B $=x$, C $=x$; total $=a+x$.
$K_p=\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{x}{a+x}p\right)^2}{\dfrac{a-x}{a+x}p}=\dfrac{x^2p}{(a+x)(a-x)}=\dfrac{x^2}{a^2-x^2}\times p$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
One half cell in a voltaic cell is constructed by dipping silver rod in $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution of unknown concentration, other half cell is Zn rod dipped in 1 molar solution of $\mathrm{ZnSO_4}$.
A voltage of 1.60 V is measured at 298 K for this cell. What is the concentration of $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ ions used in terms of $\log x$ $(x=[\mathrm{Ag^+}])$ ?
$E^\ominus_{\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}}=-0.76$ V, $E^\ominus_{\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}}=+0.80$ V, $\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.059$ V
questions.sol:
Cell: $\mathrm{Zn + 2Ag^+ \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + 2Ag}$, $E^\ominus_{cell}=0.80-(-0.76)=1.56$ V, $n=2$.
$E=1.56-\dfrac{0.059}{2}\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}]}{[\mathrm{Ag^+}]^2}=1.56+0.059\log x$.
$1.60=1.56+0.059\log x \Rightarrow \log x=\dfrac{0.04}{0.059}=\dfrac{4}{5.9}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The number of pairs among $[\mathrm{Al_2O_3, Cr_2O_3}]$, $[\mathrm{Cl_2O_7, Mn_2O_7}]$, $[\mathrm{Na_2O, V_2O_3}]$ and $[\mathrm{CO, N_2O}]$ that contain oxides of same nature (acidic, basic, neutral or amphoteric) is 4.
Statement II : Among $\mathrm{Na_2O}$, $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$, CO and $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}$, the most basic and acidic oxides are $\mathrm{Na_2O}$ and $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}$, respectively.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{Cr_2O_3}$: both amphoteric. $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}$, $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$: both acidic. $\mathrm{Na_2O}$, $\mathrm{V_2O_3}$: both basic. CO, $\mathrm{N_2O}$: both neutral.
All 4 pairs match, so Statement I is true.
$\mathrm{Na_2O}$ is strongly basic and $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7}$ (anhydride of $\mathrm{HClO_4}$) is strongly acidic; $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ is amphoteric and CO neutral. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Aluminium upon reaction with NaOH forms $[\mathrm{Al(OH)_6}]^{3-}$ ion.
Statement II : The geometry of $\mathrm{ICl_4^-}$, $\mathrm{ClO_3^-}$ and $\mathrm{IBr_2^-}$ is square planar, pyramidal and linear respectively.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{2Al + 2NaOH + 6H_2O \rightarrow 2Na^+[Al(OH)_4]^- + 3H_2}$: the product is tetrahydroxidoaluminate, $[\mathrm{Al(OH)_4}]^-$. Statement I is false.
$\mathrm{ICl_4^-}$: 4 bp + 2 lp, square planar. $\mathrm{ClO_3^-}$: 3 bp + 1 lp, pyramidal. $\mathrm{IBr_2^-}$: 2 bp + 3 lp, linear. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Presence of large number of unpaired electrons in transition metal atoms results in higher enthalpies of their atomisation.
Statement II : $d_{xy}=d_{xz}=d_{yz}<d_{x^2-y^2}=d_{z^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}=d_{z^2}<d_{xy}=d_{xz}=d_{yz}$ are the d-orbital splittings in $[\mathrm{Fe(H_2O)_6}]^{3+}$ and $[\mathrm{Ni(Cl)_4}]^{2-}$ complex ions respectively.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
More unpaired d electrons give stronger metallic bonding, so higher enthalpy of atomisation (the maxima near the middle of each series). Statement I is correct.
$[\mathrm{Fe(H_2O)_6}]^{3+}$ is octahedral: $t_{2g}$ ($d_{xy}, d_{xz}, d_{yz}$) lower than $e_g$ ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}$).
$[\mathrm{NiCl_4}]^{2-}$ is tetrahedral: $e$ ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}$) lower than $t_2$. Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements from the following
A. $[\mathrm{Fe(C_2O_4)_3}]^{3-}$ is the most stable complex among $[\mathrm{Fe(OH)_6}]^{3-}$, $[\mathrm{Fe(C_2O_4)_3}]^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{Fe(SCN)_6}]^{3-}$
B. The stability of $[\mathrm{Cu(NH_3)_4}]^{2+}$ is greater than that of $[\mathrm{Cu(en)_2}]^{2+}$
C. The hybridization of Fe in $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$ is $d^2sp^3$
D. $[\mathrm{Fe(NO_2)_3Cl_3}]^{3-}$ exhibits linkage isomerism
E. $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$ and $\mathrm{SCN^-}$ ligands are NOT ambidentate ligands
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, C, D and E
questions.sol:
A: oxalate is a chelating ligand, so $[\mathrm{Fe(C_2O_4)_3}]^{3-}$ is the most stable. True.
B: en is chelating, so $[\mathrm{Cu(en)_2}]^{2+}$ is more stable (chelate effect). False.
C: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ($3d^6$) with strong-field $\mathrm{CN^-}$ is low spin, inner orbital $d^2sp^3$. True.
D: $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$ can bind through N or O, so linkage isomerism is possible. True.
E: $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$ and $\mathrm{SCN^-}$ are ambidentate. False.
A, C and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
Purification technique		List - II
Used to separate
A. Simple distillationI. Steam volatile compound
B. Fractional distillationII. Two liquids with large difference in boiling points
C. Steam distillationIII. Liquid decomposing at its boiling point
D. Distillation under reduced pressureIV. Two liquids with close boiling points
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Simple distillation: liquids with a large difference in boiling points (II).
Fractional distillation: liquids with close boiling points (IV).
Steam distillation: steam-volatile, water-immiscible compounds (I).
Reduced-pressure distillation: liquids that decompose at their boiling point (III).
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.text:
IUPAC name of the some alkenes are given below.
Find out the correct stability order.
A. 2-Methylbut-2-ene
B. cis-But-2-ene
C. 2, 3-Dimethylbut-2-ene
D. Prop-1-ene
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

C tetrasubstituted, A trisubstituted, B disubstituted, D monosubstituted.
Order: C > A > B > D.

questions.text: Identify the correct IUPAC name of hydrocarbon $(x)$ containing three primary carbon atoms and with molar mass $72\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$.
questions.sol:
Molar mass 72 corresponds to $\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$ (1,1-dimethylcyclopropane is $\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}$, 70).
Primary carbons: n-pentane 2, 2,2-dimethylpropane 4, 2-methylbutane $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHCH_2CH_3}$ 3.

questions.text: Complete the following reaction sequence and give the name of major product 'P'.
questions.sol:
The starting compound is propanenitrile, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2C{\equiv}N}$.
(i) $\mathrm{OH^-/H_2O/\Delta}$, (ii) $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$: hydrolysis to propanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}$.
(iii) $\mathrm{Cl_2}$/red P, (iv) $\mathrm{H_2O}$: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky α-chlorination gives $\mathrm{CH_3CHClCOOH}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The condensation reaction between $\mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}O}$ and $\mathrm{H_2N-NH-C(=O)-NH_2}$ under optimum pH will produce $\mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}N-C(=O)-NH-NH_2}$
Statement II : The molecule, $\mathrm{Ph-CH(OH)(O-CH_3)}$ will generate $\mathrm{Ph-CH{=}O}$ in the presence of dilute acid.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
In semicarbazide only the terminal $\mathrm{NH_2}$ of the hydrazine part is nucleophilic (the amide $\mathrm{NH_2}$ is delocalised into C=O), so the product is the semicarbazone $\mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}N-NH-C(=O)-NH_2}$, not the structure given. Statement I is false.
$\mathrm{Ph-CH(OH)(OCH_3)}$ is a hemiacetal; in dilute acid it loses methanol to give benzaldehyde, $\mathrm{Ph-CHO}$. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Heating benzamide with bromine in an ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide will give benzylamine.
Statement II : Nitration of aniline with $\mathrm{HNO_3/H_2SO_4}$ at 288 K produces m-nitroaniline in higher amount than o-nitroaniline (pH adjusted).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Hofmann bromamide degradation removes one carbon: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2 \rightarrow C_6H_5NH_2}$ (aniline), not benzylamine. Statement I is false.
In strongly acidic medium aniline is protonated to anilinium ion (meta-directing), so nitration gives p-nitroaniline 51%, m-nitroaniline 47%, o-nitroaniline 2%. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement about tertiary structure of proteins.
options: They can be fibrous or globular in structure.
The main forces that stabilize the structure are hydrogen bonding, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces of attraction.
The structure remains intact when exposed to pH changes.
A linear polypeptide chain will convert to a secondary structure and then further folding of the secondary structure will convert to tertiary structure.
questions.sol:
The tertiary structure (fibrous or globular) arises from further folding of the secondary structure and is held by H-bonds, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces.
A change in pH disrupts these interactions and denatures the protein, so the structure does not remain intact.
The incorrect statement is the third one.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The two structures shown in the figure are two anomers of D-(+)-glucose.
Statement II : The open chain forms of D-glucose and D- fructose contain three similar chiral carbons at $C_3$, $C_4$ and $C_5$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
The two Haworth structures are identical except at C-1 (OH down in one, up in the other): they are α- and β-D-glucopyranose, the two anomers of D-(+)-glucose. Statement I is true.
Open-chain D-glucose has chiral C-2 to C-5; D-fructose (C-2 is the C=O) has chiral C-3, C-4, C-5 with the same configurations as in glucose. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A paper dipped in a dil. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ solution of 'X' upon treatment with $\mathrm{SO_2}$ gas turns into green. The compound 'X' is :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{SO_2}$ reduces acidified dichromate (orange) to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ (green):
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 3SO_2 + 2H^+ \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 3SO_4^{2-} + H_2O}$.
X is $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$.

questions.text: The total number of unpaired electrons present in the $d^3$, $d^4$ (low spin) $d^5$ (high spin), $d^6$ (high spin) and $d^7$ (low spin) octahedral complex systems is __________.

questions.text: RMgI when treated with ice cold water liberated a gas which occupied $1.4\ \mathrm{dm^3/g}$ at STP. The gas produced is further reacted with iodine in presence of $\mathrm{HIO_3}$ to give compound (X). Compound (X) in presence of Na and dry ether produced compound (Y). Molar mass of compound (Y) is __________ $\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
Molar mass of the gas $=\dfrac{22.4}{1.4}=16\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$, so the gas is $\mathrm{CH_4}$ (R = $\mathrm{CH_3}$).
$\mathrm{CH_4 + I_2 \xrightarrow{HIO_3} CH_3I}$ (X).
Wurtz reaction: $\mathrm{2CH_3I + 2Na \xrightarrow{dry\ ether} C_2H_6}$ (Y).
Molar mass of Y $=30\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$.

questions.text:
20 g hemoglobin in a 1 L aqueous solution (A) at 300 K is separated from pure water by semi permeable membrane. At equilibrium the height of solution in a tube dipped in a solution (A) is found to be 80.0 mm higher than the tube dipped in water.
The molar mass of hemoglobin is __________ $\mathrm{kg\ mol^{-1}}$. (Nearest integer)
(Given : $g=10\ \mathrm{m\ s^{-2}}$, $R=8.3\ \mathrm{kPa\ dm^3\ K^{-1}mol^{-1}}$, density of solution $=1000\ \mathrm{kg\ m^{-3}}$)
questions.sol:
Osmotic pressure $\pi=h\rho g=0.080\times1000\times10=800$ Pa $=0.8$ kPa.
$\pi=\dfrac{w}{MV}RT \Rightarrow M=\dfrac{wRT}{\pi V}=\dfrac{20\times8.3\times300}{0.8\times1}=62250\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$.
$M\approx62\ \mathrm{kg\ mol^{-1}}$.

questions.text:
At 298 K, the molar conductivity of $x$% (w/w) MX solution (aqueous) is $123.5\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$. The conductance of same solution is $1.9\times10^{-3}$ S. The value of $x$ is __________ $\times10^{-2}$.
(Given : cell constant $=1.3\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$; molar mass of MX is $75\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$, density of aqueous solution of MX at 298 K is $1.0\ \mathrm{g\ mL^{-1}}$)
questions.sol:
$\kappa=G\times\text{cell constant}=1.9\times10^{-3}\times1.3=2.47\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{S\ cm^{-1}}$.
$c=\dfrac{1000\kappa}{\Lambda_m}=\dfrac{2.47}{123.5}=0.02\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$.
1 L of solution (1000 g) contains $0.02\times75=1.5$ g MX, so $x=\dfrac{1.5}{1000}\times100=0.15=15\times10^{-2}$.

questions.text:
For a reaction $\mathrm{A\rightarrow P}$ at T K, the half life $(t_{1/2})$ is plotted as a function of initial concentration $[\mathrm{A}]_o$ of A as given below.
The value of $x$ in the given figure is __________ s (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
The graph is a straight line through the origin: $t_{1/2}\propto[\mathrm{A}]_o$, a zero-order reaction ($t_{1/2}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{A}]_o}{2k}$).
$\dfrac{x}{240}=\dfrac{1.5\times10^{-3}}{4\times10^{-3}} \Rightarrow x=90$ s.
